column3: The Hebrew names the palate rather than the mouth and coordinates the clauses with and; BSB uses as.
The Hebrew calls his arrow incurable; BSB names his wound.
The Hebrew calls them men of heart; BSB says men of understanding.
The Hebrew’s second question asks who placed the whole world without separately naming appointing Him over it; BSB supplies that description.
The Hebrew has a singular king; BSB has kings in the plural.
The Hebrew describes lifting princes’ faces; BSB describes partiality.
The Hebrew says without a hand without separately naming a human hand; BSB supplies human.
The Hebrew speaks of not appointing a man again to go to God in judgment; BSB describes no need for further examination.
The Hebrew describes striking them like wicked people; BSB says for their wickedness.
The Hebrew names nation and person without an explicit new verb for watching over them; BSB supplies watches over.
The Hebrew has a singular godless person and mentions snares of the people; BSB describes plural godless men laying snares.
